title: QA Plan Development and QA/QC Program Oversight for Vehicle Inspection Programs
capability_statement: Parsons develops, delivers, and continuously updates Quality Assurance Plans tailored to State Inspection Program requirements, with QA Managers leading the process and submitting plans for State review and approval. Our QA/QC programs comply with 40 CFR Sections 51.353, 51.366, and 51.369, and include overt, covert, telephone, real-time video, and remote record audits. Auditing infrastructure incorporates risk-based compliance monitoring, real-time data analysis with test-interruption capability, electronic record audit systems mining inspection and past audit data for triggers, and the SLTA/Audit Management and Trigger (AMT) application for monitoring deliverables and performance metrics. QA staff develop QA/QC procedures and manuals, perform data validation and QA audits, schedule and execute administrative and performance audits, and prepare audit reports across program management levels. We accommodate State final decision-making authority on QA Plan content, accept State auditing personnel access to inspection facilities during operational hours, and provide quarterly QA Plan updates within 15 days of each calendar quarter end.

Any finding of test inaccuracies will be reported to the State within one business day; corrective action and results reported within one business day after initiating corrective action, at no cost to the State.

differentiators: More than 300,000 SLTA data audits conducted, more than any other provider in the industry, supported by Parsons Qualified Equipment Technicians upholding a 25-year history of I/M auditing in North America. Risk-based compliance-monitoring system continuously analyzes millions of rows of data using effective triggers to identify anomalies, statistical patterns indicating potential noncompliant acts, and suspend test or repair activity in real time. Real-time test interruption coupled with video and audio conference review allows expert technicians to discuss inspection or repair activity as it occurs, providing both fraud detection and continuous facility staff education. Inspection lane and mechanic report cards compare testing accuracy and repair effectiveness against peer groups to streamline auditor review and identify areas of audit focus. The Auditing Covert Masking Application enables State staff to designate covert vehicles by VIN with masking transparent to inspection facilities. Updated electronic auditing system uses devices with built-in 5G cellular and Wi-Fi hardware plus smartphone support for covert and remote visual applications, supporting overt I/M, covert I/M, safety/enhanced safety, and remote record audits.
